# Implementation contract

This project is an original from-scratch re-implementation of the audio tool in
`/workspace/executable` (a build of "SoX v14.4.2").  Behaviour must be
discovered **only** by running `/workspace/executable`.  Never look for or use
the upstream source code, never decompile/disassemble/strace the binary.

## Build

`compile.sh` compiles every `src/**/*.c` into `./executable`.  Just add new `.c`
files under `src/`; no build file edits needed.  Compile with:

    bash /workspace/compile.sh

## Language / style

* C99, no external libraries other than libm and libpthread.
* `#include "sox_i.h"` gives you everything (it includes `sox.h`).
* Internal linkage for everything except the one exported symbol per module.

## Formats

Each format module `src/<mod>.c` exports exactly:

    sox_format_handler_t const *lsx_<mod>_format_fn(void);

The module name list lives in `src/formats.h`.  A module may return a handler
whose `names` array lists the primary name first then aliases, e.g.
`{"aiff", "aif", NULL}`.

Use the `lsx_read*/lsx_write*` helpers from `sox_i.h` for endian-aware I/O
(they honour `ft->encoding.reverse_bytes`).  Use `lsx_rawread`/`lsx_rawwrite`
for the actual sample coding once the header is dealt with.

## Effects

Each effect module `src/<eff>.c` exports exactly:

    sox_effect_handler_t const *lsx_<eff>_effect_fn(void);

The effect name list (and table order, which the reference's `-h` output
depends on) lives in `src/effects.h`.

`effp->priv` is pre-allocated with `handler.priv_size` bytes, zeroed.
`getopts` receives `argc`/`argv` where `argv[0]` is *not* the effect name (the
first option is `argv[0]`), matching `lsx_getopt_init(argc, argv, ..., 0, &optstate)`
usage.  Return `lsx_usage(effp)` for a usage error.

`flow` is invoked per-channel-group: unless the handler sets `SOX_EFF_MCHAN`,
the engine instantiates `effp->flows == in_signal.channels` copies and each
sees single-channel data.  With `SOX_EFF_MCHAN` there is one instance which
sees interleaved data.

## Verifying

`bash /workspace/compare.sh <args...>` runs the reference and our build with the
same arguments and diffs stdout, stderr, exit status and any produced file
byte-for-byte.  Use it constantly.

Every message the reference prints must be reproduced exactly, including
`sox: ` / `sox WARN foo: ` prefixes and trailing punctuation.  Note the
reference prints its own `argv[0]` in messages; our build must print its own.
